sec: Pathogenesis, course of untreated infection and timing of detectable markers

items.q: Early pathogenesis — match — 1) Primary infection 2) Dissemination 3) Outcome … A) Massive viraemia with wide dissemination to lymphoid organs B) Establishment of infection in GALT C) Establishment of chronic, persistent infection
items.exp: 'Primary infection → Establishment of infection in GALT → Massive viremia → Wide dissemination to lymphoid organs → Establishment of chronic, persistent infection'. (Book p1065)

items.q: Immune events — match — 1) Early response 2) Control 3) Failure … A) Partial immunologic control of virus replication B) HIV-specific immune response C) Destruction of the immune system with accelerated virus replication
items.exp: 'HIV-specific immune response', 'Partial immunologic control of virus replication' and then 'Destruction of Immune System' with 'Accelerated virus replication'. (Book p1065)

items.q: What does the page print as driving immune activation in chronic HIV?
opts: Cytokines and HIV envelope-mediated aberrant cell signalling
items.exp: 'Immune activation mediated by cytokines and HIV envelope-mediated aberrant cell signaling'. (Book p1065)

items.q: What happens to CD4 T-cell turnover, as printed?

Course of untreated HIV — match the sequence — 1) After primary infection 2) During dissemination 3) After latency 4) Terminal … A) Wide dissemination of virus with seeding of lymphoid organs B) ± acute HIV syndrome C) Constitutional symptoms, opportunistic diseases and death D) Clinical latency
items.exp: 'Primary infection → ± Acute HIV syndrome → Wide dissemination of virus, Seeding of lymphoid organs → Clinical latency → Constitutional symptoms → Opportunistic diseases → Death'. (Book p1065)

items.q: Graph axes — match the curve to its label — 1) Left axis 2) Right axis 3) Bottom axis … A) Time in weeks 0-12 then years 1-8 B) CD4+ T-lymphocyte count in cells/µL C) HIV RNA copies per mL plasma
items.exp: 'CD4+ T Lymphocyte count (cells/µL)', 'HIV RNA Copies per mL Plasma', 'Time (months after infection)' with weeks then years. (Book p1065)

items.q: Detection of HIV components — match — 1) Earliest marker 2) Next marker 3) Last … A) p24 antigen, about day 16 / 2-3 weeks B) Anti-HIV antibody C) HIV RNA, about day 10 / 1-2 weeks
items.exp: 'HIV RNA : 10th day / 1-2 weeks (earliest)'; 'p24 levels : 16th day / 2-3 weeks'; anti-HIV antibody is the last of the three curves. (Book p1065)

items.q: How early does the page print HIV RNA becoming detectable?
When does the page print p24 antigen becoming detectable?
Which chronic symptoms are printed along the untreated course?
opts: Constitutional symptoms with skin and mucous-membrane defects and systemic deficiency
items.exp: Along the course the page prints 'Constitutional' symptoms, 'Skin and mucus membrane defects' and 'Systemic deficiency', with acute and chronic lymphadenopathy and subclinical immune dysfunction. (Book p1065)

items.q: A man with a high-risk exposure 12 days ago is anxious about testing. Which marker does the page say is detectable first?
opts: None — everything is negative until 3 months
